question: Can strictly past realized outcomes from an unchanged shadow account improve entry permission, and do three causal market-environment features add value beyond recent average realized return?
clock: Original UR signal forms at T close and attempts entry only at the original next independent session open. Environment X and training label availability stop at A=T-1. A is not a new signal-formation date. No date boundary enters the decision.
shadow: Each period/board/exit has its own immutable previously completed baseline account. Only its actual entry episodes supply labels. Capacity-rejected and unfilled signals have no label. Candidate decisions never alter the shadow sample. This estimates feedback conditional on the baseline's admissions and completed exits, not all opportunities.
label: Net return fraction of a fully closed episode: cumulative net sale proceeds divided by invested amount including entry fees, minus one. Only final exitDate<=A is available. Partial exits and positions still open at A supply no return label. No terminal mark or future exit date is disclosed as a known label.

window.partialInitialWindow: Use available prior calendar slots and disclose count; no extra time gate.

training: At every A independently select labels whose final exit is in the last 126 calendar slots and whose original formation-day feature vector is complete. For each currently represented formation day give total weight one, distributing weight equally across its currently eligible closed episodes. Fit each period/board/exit independently, with no cross-period or cross-exit pooling.
standardization: Weighted training-only means and population standard deviations. A zero-variance feature becomes z=0. No clipping, return winsorization, interactions, phase labels, date variables or parameter search.
intercept: Prediction equals the same weighted training net-return mean.
ridge: Minimize sum(w_i*(y_i-alpha-beta*z_i)^2)/sum(w_i) + sum(beta_j^2). Lambda is exactly 1, intercept unpenalized. Three raw environment features, three standardized slopes, deterministic linear solve.
admission: When there are at least 20 distinct eligible formation days and the current feature vector is complete, preserve all original same-day Top5 signals only if the model predicts strictly positive net return. Zero or negative rejects that day's signals. Both candidates use the same eligible training population and support rule; otherwise both preserve the entire original schedule. Never rerank, replace an individual stock, backfill a rejected order or change exits.
execution: Every candidate gets a separate full cash/position/lot/cost replay using the original 500000 capital, five positions, 20 percent entry budget and inherited exit policy. Fees and 10bp-per-side slippage are inherited exactly. Historical raw-price, eligibility and opening-capacity limitations remain. No reconstructed deletion of baseline PnL stands in for execution.
diagnostics: All source days: train episode count, distinct formation days, label IDs/weights, model means/scales/coefficients, support/fallback, predictions and permissions.
Unmatured shadow episode counts and ages at A, separating delayed closure from known loss. Track labels excluded for unknown formation features.

Each candidate buy marked against whether its original formation was actually entered by the fixed shadow. Report candidate-only entries and their result separately, without retroactively excluding them.
Full-period net return, drawdown, exposure, costs, closed net-return distribution, win/loss magnitude, open positions and profit concentration; keep all six sources and both exits.
Year and inherited phase/9.24 cuts use carried account equity; they are descriptive cuts only. No phase reset or hindsight phase selection.
interpretation: This is one predeclared developmental feedback experiment with two entry policies, not proof of generalization. Economic zero is a decision rule, not a searched success criterion. No annual/single-trade/average-winner target or win-rate/payoff cutoff is used to select the result.
limitations: All 2022-2025 histories have already informed research; none is an untouched holdout. 2026 is excluded.
Fixed surviving source cohorts are not historical complete-market universes.
Closed-only labels can overrepresent fast losses and omit slow winners. Formation-day weights address same-day multiplicity, not serial dependence or maturity selection.
Candidate-only entries apply baseline-derived feedback outside the baseline's actually entered sample; report that shift rather than calling the model an all-opportunity forecast.
Market-volume features do not identify main-force, retail or quantitative traders.
